title: the newest item must be within the freshness window
params_pending: FRESHNESS_WINDOW_DAYS (check-feeds.mjs:20, value 7) is shared with validateFeedXml (check-feeds.mjs:71,80), which is out of this pilot's scope (UD2 brought in validateFeedJson only, one function from check-feeds.mjs, not the file). Threading it into this rule's own params would delete the shared constant and break validateFeedXml, or leave the same 7 living in two places (SEV2 again in a new costume) -- see decisions/0011 §B3. Deriving it requires bringing feed.xml into the catalog as a fourth artifact, which is a follow-up ratchet increment, not this pilot.

spec.name: JSON Feed
spec.normative_quote: JSON Feed 1.1 does not define a freshness requirement on the newest item's date_published. This is entirely a local operational policy.
spec.note: conformance_testable is false; no external spec imposes this threshold.
spec.verification_note: clause n/a -- normative_quote is a self-authored statement that JSON Feed 1.1 defines no freshness requirement on the newest item. The staleness threshold is entirely local operational policy, so there is no external clause to verify against a source.

applicability: A parsed feed.json document with at least one parseable date_published.
expectation: The newest item's date_published is not more than FRESHNESS_WINDOW_DAYS days before the evaluation instant. The comparison is strict (>), not (>=): exactly 7 days old passes.

cases.name: newest item is exactly 7 days old -- the comparison is strict (>), so this passes
multiple items out of chronological order -- the newest (by date, not array position) is fresh
